critical.issue: Product-level other_cost allocation uses plain round() with no residual absorber. For a two-line order with equal sales and other_cost_minor=1 paise, both parts round to 0 paise, so sum(products.profit_minor) exceeds snapshot.estimated_gross_profit_minor by 1 paise (observed: 26620 vs 26619). Fix: allocate the last part as (other_cost_minor - allocated) mirroring the commission allocation pattern already used two lines above.

rca of the issue: portal/metrics.py sales() distributes snap.other_cost_minor across parts using round() proportionally to part.sales_minor. Python's round() uses banker's rounding, and for two equally-priced parts with other_cost_minor=1 paise, round(0.5)=0 for both, leaving the 1 paise unallocated. The aggregated snapshot.estimated_gross_profit_minor computed in economics.snapshot() correctly deducts all 1 paise. Result: sum(products.profit_minor) - snap.estimated_gross_profit_minor = +1 paise. Reproduced with two garlic+peri-peri lines under reseller B, product_costs=1.00 each, other_cost_per_order=0.01, PERCENTAGE 10% rule scoped to B & both products (commission 2980 minor). Fix: track allocated_other in the loop and use allocated_other-absorbing residual on the final part, exactly like the existing allocated_commission pattern in the same function.
